papers.abstract_en: Basophils are rare cells best known for their role in allergy but their contribution to cancer remains poorly understood. Here, we found that basophils suppress early lung metastatic seeding in mice by enhancing antitumor CD8+ T cell immunity through inhibition of regulatory T (Treg) cells. Basophils restrain Treg cells through two complementary mechanisms: mast cell protease 8-mediated cleavage of interleukin-2 receptor α and histamine-mediated activation of the histamine H1 receptor (HRH1). HRH1 blockade with loratadine abolished Treg cell suppression and accelerated metastatic seeding in mice. In a prospective double-blind crossover trial of loratadine versus placebo enrolling 40 healthy volunteers ( IRCT20170608034390N14 ), circulating Treg cell frequency (primary outcome) increased following loratadine. Higher blood basophil counts predicted improved survival across human cancers and integrative multiomic analyses identified conserved quiescent (B0) and tumor-associated (B1) basophil states, with B0 predicting favorable outcomes. These findings identify basophils as regulators of early metastatic progression and highlight the basophil-Treg cell axis as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: PD-L1 expression in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) serves as a key predictive biomarker of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors; however, the concordance of PD-L1 expression between primary tumors and their corresponding metastatic lesions remains uncertain. We therefore performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the variability of PD-L1 expression across paired primary and metastatic NSCLC sites. METHODS: We systematically searched the Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science for eligible studies. Pooled discordance rates and patterns of mismatch were estimated using a random-effects model, and subgroup analyses were conducted according to PD-L1 cutoff, antibody clone, and metastatic site. RESULTS: Fifteen studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria, encompassing 1,029 matched primary-metastatic sample pairs from 1,014 patients with NSCLC. The pooled analysis revealed an overall PD-L1 discordance rate of 21% between primary tumors and corresponding metastases (95% CI: 18%-25%). Notably, transitions from PD-L1-positive primary tumors to PD-L1-negative metastatic lesions occurred more frequently (26%, 95% CI: 22%-30%) than the reverse pattern, from negative primaries to positive metastases (18%, 95% CI: 12%-24%). Discordance of similar magnitude was observed across PD-L1 positivity thresholds and antibody clones and in both lymph node and brain metastases, although the site-specific estimates are exploratory. DISCUSSION: In patients with NSCLC, PD-L1 expression frequently differs between primary and metastatic lesions, with a greater tendency for expression to decrease at metastatic sites. These findings indicate that PD-L1 results obtained from an archival primary tumor should be interpreted with caution when they are used to inform treatment of metastatic disease. Whether repeat testing of metastatic tissue improves patient selection or immunotherapy outcomes has not been demonstrated and requires prospective evaluation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO, identifier CRD42022336191.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Pulse oximetry may overestimate oxygen saturation in individuals with darker skin pigmentation, potentially reducing detection of desaturation during sleep-disordered breathing. OBJECTIVES: To assess racial/ethnic differences in desaturation-based obstructive event detection and cardiovascular risk, and evaluate heart-rate response as an oximetry-independent marker for risk stratification. METHODS: We analyzed participants without cardiovascular disease in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis(MESA) and Sleep Heart Health Study(SHHS). We modeled desaturation-based AHI relative to airflow-defined AHI and examined AHI-ΔHR6, defined by respiratory events with a heart-rate increase ≥6 beats/min. Adjusted Cox models evaluated associations with a composite outcome, major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality(MACE/mortality). MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Black participants had 21% and 20% lower proportions of airflow-defined events meeting the ≥4% desaturation criterion than White participants in MESA (ratio 0.79[95% CI,0.68-0.93]; p = 0.003) and SHHS (0.80[0.68-0.94]; p = 0.008), respectively. No other racial/ethnic group showed a lower proportion of airflow-defined events meeting desaturation criteria than White participants. AHI-ΔHR6 event detection was similar between Black and White participants in both cohorts. In Whites participants, desaturation-based events were associated with MACE/mortality in MESA but not in SHHS, while desaturation-based AHI measures were not significantly associated with MACE/mortality in Black individuals in either cohort. In contrast, AHI-ΔHR6 was associated with MACE/mortality in MESA (HR 1.33[1.09-1.63];p=0.006) and SHHS (1.26[1.02-1.55]; p = 0.033). CONCLUSIONS: Desaturation-based scoring identified a lower proportion of reduced flow events in Black than White participants, whereas heart-rate-response-based event detection was similar across groups, suggesting oximetry-related under-detection in individuals with darker pigment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The survival benefit of elective nodal irradiation (ENI) over involved-field irradiation (IFI) in ESCC remains unclear, suggesting uncharacterized systemic costs. Radiation-induced lymphopenia (RIL) is increasingly recognized as an adverse prognostic factor that may undermine antitumor immunity. We investigated whether ENI increases EDRIC, a validated dosimetric biomarker of RIL, and whether EDRIC mediates ENI's survival disadvantage via immune injury. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 279 ESCC patients treated with definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (2011- 2015). EDRIC was computed using a validated model incorporating mean lung, heart, and body doses and fraction number. Inverse probability weighting balanced 14 baseline covariates. Causal mediation analysis within the counterfactual framework quantified the proportion of the total effect of radiotherapy field strategy on OS mediated by EDRIC. RESULTS: ENI significantly elevated EDRIC compared with IFI (8.17 vs. 7.42 Gy; P = 0.01). High EDRIC (>7.8 Gy) independently predicted worse OS (HR = 1.746; P<0.001), PFS, and LRFFS. The IFI- low EDRIC subgroup achieved the best 10- year OS (28.3%), significantly superior to both IFI- high EDRIC (12.0%; P = 0.004) and ENI- H group (13.5%; P = 0.024). ENI increased mortality risk by 52% (total effect Rte=1.52; P = 0.016). Causal mediation analysis revealed that EDRIC mediated 33% of this effect (indirect effect Rtnie=1.13; 95% CI: 1.02-1.29; P = 0.015). CONCLUSION: Elevated EDRIC was statistically associated with one-third of ENI's excess mortality risk. Applying the exploratory 7.8 Gy median cutoff, low-EDRIC IFI was associated with superior long-term survival, suggesting a potential immunoprotective strategy that warrants further validation. These findings support optimizing radiotherapy field design to preserve host immunity in future combination regimens.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer harboring epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations exhibits marked heterogeneity in clinical responses to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs), indicating that co-occurring genetic alterations critically influence therapeutic outcomes. However, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we modeled frequent EGFR co-alterations using CRISPR-mediated gene knockout and Tet-On-based gene overexpression in two EGFR-mutant cell lines. Functional screening across cell lines and patient-derived organoids revealed that concurrent loss of retinoblastoma 1 (RB1) significantly reduced sensitivity to EGFR-TKIs. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses further demonstrated that RB1 deficiency induced extensive metabolic reprogramming, leading to decreased intracellular crotonyl-CoA levels and reduced histone crotonylation. Among multiple crotonylation sites, histone H3 lysine 23 crotonylation (H3K23cr) emerged as a critical determinant of EGFR-TKI responsiveness. Mechanistically, decreased H3K23cr was associated with transcriptional repression of PEBP1 and reduced expression of the PEBP1-encoded Raf kinase inhibitor protein (RKIP), thereby sustaining RAF/MEK/ERK pathway activation and attenuating EGFR-TKI efficacy. Importantly, pharmacological restoration of histone crotonylation or inhibition of MAPK signaling effectively resensitized EGFR/RB1 co-mutant models to EGFR-TKIs. Taken together, our findings identify a metabolic-epigenetic mechanism linking RB1 loss to reduced histone crotonylation and EGFR-TKI resistance, highlighting therapeutically actionable vulnerabilities in EGFR/RB1 co-mutant lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Antihyperglycemic agents may influence infection risk through distinct immunometabolic pathways. We compared glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) in patients with COPD and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). METHODS: This population-based, active-comparator, new-user cohort study used the TriNetX Global Network. Adults aged 40-100 years with COPD and T2DM who initiated a GLP-1RA or DPP-4i between 2007 and 2019 were included. Propensity score matching (1:1) adjusted for demographics, BMI, HbA1c, COPD severity proxies, comorbidities, and medications. The primary outcome was sepsis; secondary outcomes were pneumonia, severe sepsis, and all-cause mortality, assessed at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. RESULTS: Before matching, 21,622 patients started a GLP-1RA and 67,259 a DPP-4i; after matching, 20,074 remained in each group with balanced characteristics (all standardized mean differences <0.10). Compared with DPP-4i users, GLP-1RA users had a significantly lower risk of sepsis at 1 year (hazard ratio [HR] 0.852; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.770-0.942). The risks of secondary outcomes at 1 year were numerically lower in the GLP-1RA group, with statistically significant reductions in pneumonia (HR 0.729; 95% CI 0.671-0.792) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.656; 95% CI 0.587-0.732), while the association with severe sepsis did not reach statistical significance (HR 0.891; 95% CI 0.770-1.033). CONCLUSION: In patients with COPD and T2DM, initiation of GLP-1RAs was associated with lower risks of sepsis, pneumonia, and all-cause mortality compared with DPP-4is. However, given the observational design, causality cannot be established and residual confounding remains a potential limitation. While these findings suggest potential benefits of GLP-1RAs beyond glycemic control, further confirmation through randomized controlled trials is warranted to guide clinical decision-making.

papers.authors: Gilboa-Sagy H, Shitrit D, Guber E, Eyre A, Epstein Shochet G, Romem A
papers.affiliation_highlight: Pulmonary Department, Meir Medical Center, Kfar Saba, Israel.
papers.results: 加用注射器抽吸物后诊断阳性率由58.3%升至62.9%（+4.6%，p=0.016）；样本充分性维持不变（98.7%）；排除恶性肿瘤的准确率由85.4%升至88.1%，差异无统计学意义（p=0.125）；TBNA标本与注射器标本一致性87.9%；7例诊断（含4例恶性肿瘤）仅依靠注射器抽吸物确立
papers.authors_conclusion: Cytological analysis of suction-syringe aspirate modestly but significantly enhances EBUS-TBNA diagnostic yield and should be considered in routine practice.
papers.ai_note: 仅42.5%（151/355）存在可见抽吸物，结论实际限于该亚组，人群限定松动；基线诊断阳性率58.3%明显低于文献中EBUS-TBNA常规水平，提示本中心操作或判定标准可能偏严，增量+4.6%的可推广性存疑；准确率改善（85.4%→88.1%）未达统计学显著（p=0.125），但结论仍建议纳入常规实践，存在以显著的次要/替代终点（诊断阳性率）支撑临床推荐的倾向；单中心配对设计，缺乏外部验证

pico.ic: 常规EBUS-TBNA标本 + 注射器抽吸物细胞学检查 vs 常规EBUS-TBNA标本（同一患者配对比较）

papers.reason: 影响EBUS-TBNA操作流程与标本处理决策——为是否回收注射器抽吸物送细胞学提供直接证据，同时其小幅增量与低基线阳性率可作为评估该技术真实收益的参照
papers.abstract_en: BackgroundDuring endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA), visible aspirated material may accumulate in the suction syringe but is typically discarded.ObjectiveTo assess whether cytological examination of suction-syringe aspirate improves the diagnostic performance of EBUS-TBNA.DesignProspective, single-center, paired-sample diagnostic study.MethodsPooled aspirated material was preserved in formalin and analyzed cytologically alongside routine EBUS-TBNA specimens. Diagnostic yield, adequacy, and accuracy were compared with/without syringe aspirate analysis.ResultsAmong 355 screened patients, 151 (42.5%) had visible syringe aspirate and were included. Adding syringe aspirate increased diagnostic yield from 58.3% to 62.9% (+4.6%, p=0.016). Sample adequacy remained unchanged (98.7%). Accuracy for excluding malignancy improved from 85.4% to 88.1%, although not significantly (p=0.125). Concordance between TBNA and syringe samples was 87.9%. Seven diagnoses, including four malignancies, were established exclusively from syringe aspirate.ConclusionCytological analysis of suction-syringe aspirate modestly but significantly enhances EBUS-TBNA diagnostic yield and should be considered in routine practice.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Given the uncertain future and potential changes to Medicaid, we sought to evaluate the impact of the 2014 Affordable Care Act Medicaid Expansion on non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) stage at diagnosis and rates of surgery for patients diagnosed with clinical stage I disease. METHODS: The National Cancer Database was used to identify patients diagnosed with NSCLC between 2004 and 2022, stratified by diagnosis timing (pre- vs post Medicaid expansion) and state expansion status. Demographic, clinical, and treatment variables were compared across time periods and expansion status using chi-square tests (categorical) and t-tests (continuous). RESULTS: Among 1,585,967 patients diagnosed with NSCLC, during the study period, 37.9% (n=600,411) were diagnosed pre-expansion and 62.1% (n=982,556) post-expansion (Table 1). A notable shift toward earlier stage of diagnosis was identified in the post-expansion era: only 17.4% (n=85,351) of patients were with cIA NSCLC pre-expansion compared to 27.3% (n=243,434) post-expansion. This shift was additionally more pronounced in expansion states (28.1% [n=135,686] vs 26.2% [n=107,748], p<0.001). Correspondingly, surgical resection for cIA NSCLC increased from 48.4% (n=56,590) pre-expansion to 61.3% (n=144,433) post-expansion, with higher rates of surgery in expansion states vs. non-expansion states (62.4% [n=82,615] vs 59.9% [n=61,818], p<0.0010). CONCLUSIONS: Medicaid expansion was associated with increased early-stage NSCLC diagnosis and surgical treatment with larger gains in expansion states, suggesting a direct effect on access and screening. As Medicaid policy evolves, continued advocacy is vital to ensure early detection and adequate care delivery for patients with NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Exposure to respirable coal mine dust causes coal workers' pneumoconiosis (CWP). Despite regulatory efforts, progressive massive fibrosis (PMF), the most severe form of pneumoconiosis persists, particularly in Central Appalachia. This study evaluated pneumoconiosis prevalence among underground coal miners by occupation during 1991-2024. METHODS: The study analyzed data from 30,319 underground miners in the Coal Workers Health Surveillance Program (CWHSP) from 1991-2024. Pneumoconiosis was identified from chest radiographs using standardized classifications. Disease prevalence was compared across mining occupations and geographic regions, with adjustment for underground mining tenure. RESULTS: Continuous miner operators (CMOs) and roof bolters experienced the highest prevalence of disease. Compared with miners who never held these occupations, adjusted prevalence of CWP was higher among CMOs (PR = 1.8; 95% CI: 1.6-2.0) and roof bolters (PR = 1.4; 95% CI: 1.3-1.6). PMF prevalence was also elevated among CMOs (PR = 3.0; 95% CI: 2.3-4.0) and roof bolters (PR = 1.4; 95% CI: 1.1-1.9). CWP prevalence was 8.4% in Central Appalachia versus 1.5% in the rest of U. S., while PMF prevalence was 1.3% versus 0.1%. After adjustment for tenure, Central Appalachian miners had 3.9 times the prevalence of CWP (95% CI: 3.4-4.5) and 10 times the prevalence of PMF (95% CI: 5.7-17.5). DISCUSSION: CMOs and roof bolters experienced the highest prevalence of pneumoconiosis, consistent with their classification as MSHA-designated "dusty" occupations. Markedly higher disease prevalence across all occupations in Central Appalachia indicates persistent hazardous dust exposures and underscores the need for continued prevention and surveillance efforts.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of accelerated biological aging characterized by progressive lung function decline, emphysema progression and multiple age-related comorbidities. Current therapies improve symptoms and reduce exacerbations but have limited effects on disease progression. Metformin has demonstrated anti-aging properties through modulation of pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence, making it a potential disease-modifying treatment in COPD. METHODS: AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COPD) is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial conducted in anonymous. A total of 212 patients with clinically stable COPD, centrilobular emphysema on computed tomography, post-bronchodilator FEV1 40%-70% predicted and accelerated FEV1 decline (>40 mL·year-1) will be randomized (1:1) to receive metformin (850 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 36 months in addition to standard COPD treatment. Assessments include pulmonary function, chest computed tomography, exercise capacity, health status, muscle strength, body composition, age associated comorbidities development and aging-related biomarkers.The primary endpoint is the annual rate of FEV1 decline over 36 months. Secondary endpoints include emphysema progression, changes in diffusing capacity, COPD Assessment Test score, 6-minute walk distance, BODE index, handgrip strength, exacerbations, major cardiovascular events, cancer incidence and renal dysfunction. CONCLUSIONS: AMICO is the first randomized trial specifically designed to evaluate metformin as a gerotherapeutic and disease-modifying intervention in COPD. The study may provide novel evidence supporting geroscience-based approaches to slow disease progression and improve long-term outcomes in patients with COPD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The long-term risk of clinical new-onset pulmonary fibrosis (PF) and its various downstream impacts following SARS-CoV-2 infection remain incompletely characterized in existing literature. METHODS: A retrospective cohort was analyzed using Montefiore Health System electronic health record data over 4.5 years (March 2020-August 2024). Hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients without prior PF diagnosis were matched 1:2 to COVID-19 negative controls. New-onset PF and subsequent downstream impacts were identified by diagnostic ICD-10 codes. Covariate balance was assessed and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) models were used to estimate PF risk and logistic and Poisson regression models were used to assess post-PF secondary outcomes. Sensitivity analyses included multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional-hazard models, inverse probability weighting and analyses using a pre-pandemic historical control. FINDINGS: After propensity score matching, both hospitalized COVID-19 patients (sHR = 2.05; 95% CI [1.69-2.4]) and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients (sHR = 2.33; 95% CI [1.88-2.88]) demonstrated significantly increased risk of PF when compared to COVID-19 negative controls over up to 4.5-year follow-up period. In patients with new-onset PF, prior hospitalization with COVID-19 has associated with higher odds of pneumonia (OR = 4.84 [3.50-6.67]), bronchiolitis (OR = 3.45 [1.12-8.81]), respiratory failure (OR = 3.76 [2.72-5.16]), asthma exacerbation (OR = 2.54 [1.36-4.46]) and COPD exacerbation (OR = 2.91 [1.80-4.58]), whereas non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients exhibited increased odds of pneumonia (OR = 1.98 [1.25-3.06]) and asthma exacerbation (OR = 2.06[1.00-3.86]). Similarly, hospitalized COVID-19 patients showed increased risk of PH (RR = 1.66[1.01-2.71]) and non-hospitalized patients showed an increased risk of PE (RR = 2.68[1.14-6.35]). INTERPRETATIONS: In a diverse cohort with up to 4.5 years follow-up, we found both hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients have a higher long-term risk of new-onset PF and higher burden of subsequent downstream respiratory complications compared to matched non-COVID-19 controls. These findings demonstrate post-COVID-19 PF as a relevant and clinically significant outcome and suggest the need for long-term surveillance, risk stratification, and targeted intervention.

papers.abstract_en: Clot in transit, defined as a mobile right heart thrombus, is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of venous thromboembolism. Its presence in acute pulmonary embolism is associated with high mortality and hemodynamic instability. Diagnosis relies primarily on echocardiography, with adjunctive roles for computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance. Management remains challenging due to the absence of randomized trials. Treatment options include anticoagulation alone, systemic thrombolysis, surgical embolectomy, and catheter-based interventions, with outcomes favoring active reperfusion in unstable patients. Multidisciplinary decision-making is essential, and ongoing research aims to clarify optimal strategies to improve survival in this high-risk population.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary embolism is a life-threatening condition requiring prompt anticoagulation to prevent clot propagation and recurrence. Risk stratification guides therapy, with systemic thrombolysis reserved for high-risk patients and selected intermediate-high risk cases due to significant bleeding risk. Direct oral anticoagulants are preferred for most low and intermediate-low risk patients, while low-molecular-weight heparin and unfractionated heparin remain critical for higher- risk or procedurally complex cases. Management of bleeding complications necessitates rapid intervention, reversal when available, and coordinated multidisciplinary care.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality despite advances in targeted therapy and immune checkpoint blockade. NLRP3-associated inflammation has attracted increasing interest in NSCLC, yet interpretation of the available evidence remains challenging because molecular expression, inflammasome activation, cytokine processing, pyroptotic execution and pathway dependence are frequently considered together. Here, we present a structured narrative review and an evidence framework that separates the biological event directly measured from the level of NLRP3-specific mechanistic support, while independently considering cellular source, disease relevance and treatment context. Current evidence indicates that NLRP3-specific mechanistic dependence in NSCLC has been demonstrated only in selected experimental settings, particularly treatment-conditioned macrophage models. Treatment-naïve human evidence reveals compartment-specific inflammasome-associated responses in alveolar macrophages and peripheral leukocytes but does not establish NLRP3 dependence. Tumour-cell studies support treatment-induced inflammasome- and pyroptosis-associated phenotypes, although causal attribution to NLRP3 is often incomplete. Single-cell and spatial studies mainly identify NLRP3-related transcriptional states or candidate microenvironmental niches and cannot, by themselves, demonstrate functional inflammasome activation or NLRP3-dependent interactions. Clinical trials targeting IL-1β provide evidence for downstream inflammatory modulation but do not directly evaluate NLRP3 inhibition. Overall, current evidence supports context-dependent NLRP3-associated biology in NSCLC rather than a uniform biomarker or therapeutic target. Future studies integrating cell-resolved localisation, activation-specific measurements, pathway perturbation and longitudinal validation are required to determine whether clinically relevant NLRP3-dependent states can be reproducibly identified.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI), and lung cancer have been identified as major respiratory diseases. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is an important respiratory risk factor, but evidence on life-course exposure to individual constituents and associated biological signatures remains limited. METHODS: Among 47,737 participants from UK Biobank, birth-to-baseline residential histories were linked to annual concentrations of PM2.5, sulfate (SO42-), nitrate (NO3-), ammonium (NH4+), organic carbon (OC), and elemental carbon (EC) estimated by the Community Multiscale Air Quality model during 1930-2010. Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) per interquartile range (IQR) increase, and quantile g-computation to estimate mixture effects. Exposure- and disease-associated biomarkers were screened, followed by mediation analyses, protein functional enrichment, and metabolite categorization. RESULTS: During 13-14 years of follow-up, each IQR increase in PM2.5 was associated with higher risks of COPD (HR: 1.138, 95% CI 1.069-1.211), asthma (HR: 1.171, 95% CI 1.105-1.241), LRTI (HR: 1.046, 95% CI 1.002-1.091), and lung cancer (HR: 1.193, 95% CI 1.064-1.337). SO42- and EC were positively associated with all four outcomes. Mixture analyses showed significant joint associations with COPD and asthma. Candidate proteins were enriched in immune-inflammatory, cell adhesion, PI3K-Akt, and cytokine/chemokine pathways, whereas candidate metabolites were predominantly lipoprotein-related. CONCLUSIONS: Life-course exposures to PM2.5 and its constituents were associated with increased respiratory disease risks and candidate biological signatures. These findings highlight the relevance of PM2.5 chemical composition to major respiratory diseases and future mechanistic studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) is a severe pulmonary manifestation of chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Evidence for extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) in this setting has not been systematically appraised. METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to 30 September 2026 for studies reporting pulmonary outcomes of ECP for BOS or lung cGVHD after HCT. Forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), lung response, survival, corticosteroid exposure, and safety were extracted, and risk of bias was appraised. RESULTS: Six studies (68 ECP-treated patients) were included: four BOS-specific cohorts and two cGVHD cohorts with lung subgroups. None was randomized; three were retrospective, including the only controlled study, and three single-arm series did not clearly report their design. Short-term FEV1 response or stabilization occurred in 67% (6/9) and 88% (7/8) in two cohorts, but in one only 25% (2/8) remained stable at 12 months. In the controlled study (26 ECP vs 26 matched controls), FEV1 decline slowed similarly in both groups (between-group P = 0.33), whereas ECP was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio 0.1) and less prednisone use >5 mg/day (23% vs 54%). Lung responses in cGVHD cohorts were 22% (2/9) and 0% (0/3). CONCLUSIONS: Evidence for ECP in HCT-associated BOS is limited to small observational studies at high risk of bias. With ruxolitinib, belumosudil, and axatilimab available and pirfenidone, nintedanib, and abatacept under study, ECP is best positioned as an adjunct for selected patients. Prospective comparative studies are needed.

papers.abstract_en: Epidemiological evidence linking asthma to lung cancer risk remains contradictory, presenting asthma as either a risk factor or a protective condition. We hypothesize that this heterogeneity stems from the temporal dynamics of inflammatory response and host genetic background. Using ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma models, we identify a temporal shift in immune effectors driving post-asthmatic tumorigenesis. During acute airway inflammation, eosinophil infiltration accelerates tumor growth across mouse strains. Following resolution, however, tumorigenic outcomes in recovery diverge along genetic lines. Prior asthma reshapes chromatin landscapes of bone marrow myeloid progenitors, establishing innate immune memory that differentially programs monocytes across strains. In C57BL/6 mice, trained monocytes adopt oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), acquiring a suppressive, tissue-remodeling phenotype that promotes tumor progression. Conversely, BALB/c-trained monocytes utilize glycolysis to maintain a pro-phagocytic state, enabling tumor clearance. These findings delineate a biphasic mechanism wherein temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte metabolic reprogramming.

papers.abstract_en: Sepsis-associated lung injury arises from a dysregulated host response to infection, but the organelle-level mechanisms linking microbial sensing to alveolar-capillary barrier failure remain incompletely resolved. This Review proposes lysosomal pH dysregulation as a candidate, context-dependent signal-amplifying hub rather than a universal initiating event. We synthesize evidence involving V-ATPase-dependent acidification, ClC-7/OSTM1-mediated chloride homeostasis, TMEM175-dependent ion conductance, mTORC1-TFEB signaling, mitochondrial stress, mitochondria-lysosome contact-site proton transfer, and autophagy-lysosome function while distinguishing direct organelle pH measurements from non-equivalent readouts such as membrane permeabilization, cathepsin redistribution, LysoTracker intensity, and autophagic flux. Of 21 formally appraised mechanistic axes, only 2 met Level I criteria; most evidence was Level III or IV and therefore extrapolative or hypothesis-generating. Across macrophages, epithelial cells, pulmonary endothelial cells, and fibroblasts, lysosomal dysfunction may impair pathogen clearance and cellular quality control while amplifying inflammatory signaling and alveolar-capillary barrier injury. We therefore position lysosomal pH homeostasis as a testable mechanistic and stratification axis whose relevance is likely to vary by compartment, cell type, and disease stage.

papers.authors: Shi Y, Jiang H, Pu S, Liu Y, Wang Y, Liu W

papers.results: ln-CALLY 每升高 1 个单位，校正后 COPD 风险降低 17%（HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.81-0.85, P < 0.001）；最高四分位 vs 最低四分位风险降低 41%（HR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.54-0.64, P < 0.001）。RCS 分析显示显著 L 型关系；拐点 ln-CALLY = 7.00，阈值以下每升高 1 个单位风险降低 19%（HR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.78-0.83, P < 0.001），阈值以上关联无统计学显著性（未报告具体 HR 数值）。关联在 <65 岁人群中更明显；敏感性分析结果一致。平均随访 13.6 年内共 6618 例新发 COPD 事件。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index has shown prognostic value in various chronic conditions, but its prospective association with incident chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and potential non-linear dose-response patterns remain unexplored. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 292,945 UK Biobank participants. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate the association between the natural-log-transformed CALLY (ln-CALLY) index and incident COPD. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) curves and two-segment Cox regression were applied to characterize non-linear associations and identify inflection points. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess robustness. RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 13.6 years, 6618 incident COPD events occurred. Each one-unit increment in ln-CALLY was associated with a 17% lower risk of COPD in the fully adjusted model (HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.81-0.85, P < 0.001). The highest quartile exhibiting a 41% risk reduction versus the lowest (HR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.54-0.64, P < 0.001). RCS analysis revealed a significant L-shaped relationship. Threshold effect analysis identified an inflection point at ln-CALLY = 7.00; below this threshold, each one-unit increase was associated with a 19% risk reduction (HR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.78-0.83, P < 0.001), whereas above the threshold the association was non-significant. The inverse association was more pronounced in participants aged <65 years. Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. CONCLUSION: The CALLY index exhibits a significant L-shaped association with incident COPD risk, characterized by a pronounced protective effect below ln-CALLY = 7.00 and a risk plateau above this threshold. These findings support the broader concept that immuno-nutritional status is a determinant of respiratory health.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In Australia, non-pharmaceutical interventions introduced early in 2020 to curtail the spread of COVID-19 resulted in the temporary elimination of influenza. We used data from this influenza-free period (2021) to validate influenza mortality burden predictions from time-series models. METHODS: Time-series models were parameterised with routinely collected health data from 2010 to 2019 (pre-pandemic) and from 2010 to 2019 plus 2021 (pandemic-inclusive). These models were used to predict influenza A- and influenza B-associated mortality rates in Queensland between 2010 and 2019. Mortality estimates were made in persons < 65 and ≥ 65 years for pneumonia and influenza (P&I) and respiratory illnesses as contributory mortality causes and for all-cause mortality. RESULTS: The models predicted consistent mortality rates for influenza B. However, the pandemic-inclusive model for individuals ≥ 65 years predicted influenza A-associated P&I mortality of 32.1 per 100,000 person-years (95% prediction interval [PI]: 25.9, 39.6), significantly higher than the pre-pandemic model estimate of 17.6 (95% PI: 13.4, 23.6). A similar, non-significant difference occurred for respiratory mortality. CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest that time-series modelling may underestimate the true burden of influenza-A mortality among the elderly. Further studies are needed to confirm this finding and establish the conditions under which the time-series regression approach may be reliable.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cognitive difficulties are prevalent in patients with sarcoidosis and are poorly understood. We examined associations between clinical disease characteristics and cognitive dysfunction, measured by Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) in an unselected cohort of patients with sarcoidosis. METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective analysis of 171 patients with sarcoidosis, excluding those with neurosarcoidosis or incomplete data. The primary outcome was cognitive dysfunction defined as MoCA ≤ 25. Disease burden measures included number and type of immunosuppressive medication classes, disease duration, organ involvement, and fatigue. Quality of life was assessed with the 36-Item Short Form Survey (SF-36) as a secondary outcome. RESULTS: Cognitive dysfunction was present in 39.2% of our sample, despite a relatively young age (median age at baseline of 57 and 75th percentile of 64). Use of any immunosuppressive therapy was associated with a 1.38 point (p = 0.002) decrease in MoCA score. This association was driven by corticosteroids with ever users having scores an average of a 1.15 (p = 0.005) point lower MoCA than never users; however, duration of corticosteroid use was not significantly associated with MoCA scores. Disease duration, organ system involvement, and fatigue severity were not related to cognitive performance. Stronger cognitive performance on the MoCA was associated with better physical quality of life by the SF-36. DISCUSSION: In our cohort, 39.2% of patients had cognitive dysfunction. Immunosuppressive treatment, especially corticosteroid use, was associated with lower cognitive performance. Whether this reflects sarcoidosis-driven cognitive dysfunction or is confounded by corticosteroid-related neuropsychiatric effects remains unclear.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are common but often underrecognized in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), while evidence from resource-limited settings remains scarce. This study assessed their prevalence and correlates among patients with COPD attending a tertiary pulmonary clinic in Damascus, Syria. METHODS: This cross-sectional, single-center convenience-sample study included 249 patients with COPD at Al-Mouwassat Hospital. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using validated Arabic versions of the GAD-7 and PHQ-9. Clinically relevant symptoms were defined as GAD-7 ≥10 and PHQ-9 ≥10. Spirometric impairment was characterized using FEV1% predicted. The GAD-specific challenge burden score ranged from 0 to 4 and was modeled as a continuous predictor. Bivariate analyses were followed by multinomial logistic regression for GAD-7 severity and proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression for PHQ-9 severity, with sensitivity analyses using GOLD-based FEV1 categories and binary symptom thresholds. RESULTS: Clinically relevant anxiety and depressive symptoms were present in 30.9% and 73.9% of participants, respectively. Each one-point increase in the GAD-specific challenge burden score was associated with mild anxiety (adjusted OR, 7.07; 95% CI, 3.36-14.89) and moderate-to-severe anxiety (adjusted OR, 26.95; 95% CI, 10.32-70.41). Older age and lower FEV1% predicted were additionally associated with moderate-to-severe anxiety. Greater depressive symptom severity was associated with lower FEV1% predicted, COPD duration ≥1 year, and difficulty performing daily tasks. Sensitivity analyses showed consistent findings. CONCLUSION: Anxiety and depressive symptoms were common in this outpatient cohort. Both spirometric impairment and patient-reported symptom and functional burden were associated with psychological symptom severity, supporting multidimensional COPD assessment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry (PRISm) is increasingly recognized as a potential precursor to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, evidence on its relevance in Lebanon and neighboring countries remains limited. This study aimed to estimate PRISm prevalence, identify associated factors, and assess its relationship with quality of life (QoL) among adults. METHODS: A cross-sectional study using multistage cluster sampling was conducted in two major governorates (Beirut and Mount Lebanon) in 2025. Participants were classified as having normal pulmonary function tests (PFTs) with FEV1 (forced expiratory volume in 1 sec)/FVC (forced vital capacity) ≥ 0.7 and FEV1 ≥ 80%, PRISm with FEV1/FVC ≥ 0.7 and FEV1 < 80% post-bronchodilator, COPD as FEV1/FVC < 70% post-bronchodilator, or other patterns. Data included sociodemographic, clinical, lifestyle, and QoL using the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ). A multinomial regression analysis was conducted to identify factors associated with each spirometry pattern, mainly PRISm, while a multiple linear regression was used to examine factors associated with the QoL. An alpha of 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: The mean age of the 760 participants was 60 years (51.3% females, 53.4% current smokers). PRISm prevalence was 10.1% (95% CI: 8.1-12.5). PRISm were older (adjusted OR (95% CI) = 1.03 (1.01-1.05); p=0.042), had greater cumulative cigarette smoking (1.007 (1.001-1.01; p=0.028), and were more likely to report wheeze (2.64 (1.34-5.20); p=0.005) versus normal PFT. PRISm was not significantly associated with worse QoL, whereas COPD was associated with poorer QoL. CONCLUSION: PRISm may represent an important respiratory phenotype in this LMIC, associated with older age, cumulative smoking, and wheeze, supporting the role of spirometry-based early detection and smoking cessation in at-risk populations. PRISm was not significantly associated with QoL impairment, in contrast to COPD, highlighting the substantial patient-reported burden of the latter. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the natural history of PRISm and guide prevention and management strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer, the deadliest malignant tumor worldwide, consists predominantly of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and accounts for most cancer-related deaths; its aggressive metastatic nature severely compromises treatment outcomes and overall survival. Abelson tyrosine kinase (ABL), a key regulator of metastasis across multiple tumor types, has emerged as a promising therapeutic target. Gramicidin's effects on NSCLC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion were assessed using CCK-8, colony formation, Transwell, and wound healing assays. ABL protein levels were analyzed using Western blot (WB). The effects of ABL expression on MMP9 levels and cellular migration and invasion were examined in ABL-knockdown cells using gelatin zymography, WB, Transwell, and wound healing assays. ABL-overexpressing cells were treated with gramicidin to examine gramicidin's suppression of the ABL-MMP9 axis using WB, Transwell, and wound healing assays. In a BALB/c nude mouse model of lung metastasis established via tail vein injection of tumor cells, we evaluated the inhibitory effects of gramicidin on metastatic nodule formation in vivo and its influence on ABL and MMP9 expressions. Gramicidin significantly suppressed lung cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. ABL was upregulated in human lung cancer cells and could be effectively suppressed by gramicidin treatment. Gramicidin downregulated MMP9 expression by suppressing ABL protein expression, thereby attenuating lung cancer metastasis. In vivo, gramicidin treatment reduced the number of lung metastatic nodules and simultaneously downregulated ABL and MMP9 proteins in lung tissue, effects that were partially reversed by ABL overexpression. This study revealed the molecular mechanism by which gramicidin inhibits lung cancer metastasis through suppression of the ABL-MMP9 axis, providing a theoretical foundation for developing gramicidin-based anti-metastatic strategies.

papers.results: 精神分裂症患病率高于一般人群：36/186（19%）个体、97/328（30%）次住院；精神分裂症组更年轻（66.6 vs 72.5岁，p=0.001）；当前吸烟者比例更高（75% vs 42.7%，p=0.005）；住院时间更短（LOS 6 vs 9天，p=0.043）；无创通气时长更短（3 vs 5天，p=0.021）；NIV停用原因两组间无显著差异；再入院率更高（44.4% vs 24.0%，p=0.025）；死亡年龄更低（67.3 vs 77.4岁，p<0.001）。摘要未报告任何效应量的95%CI或校正后HR。

These findings suggest that schizophrenia is an at-risk subgroup in AHRF, highlighting the need for collaborative action.

pico.p: COPD需无创通气（NIV）治疗急性高碳酸血症呼吸衰竭（AHRF）的住院患者；单中心2017-01-01至2024-12-31共186人/328次住院（排除2020-01-01至2022-12-31 COVID-19期间），其中精神分裂症36人（19%）、97次住院（30%）

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Limited data describe outcomes in people with comorbid schizophrenia when admitted with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure (AHRF). This study compared outcomes in people with COPD requiring non-invasive ventilation (NIV), with and without schizophrenia, to identify priorities for intervention and research. METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study from a single Australian quaternary referral hospital of people with COPD requiring NIV for AHRF over 5 years from 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2024, excluding admissions between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted usual practices. Primary outcomes were length of stay (LOS) and NIV duration (days). Secondary outcomes included NIV discontinuation reason, challenges to NIV and readmission. Descriptive and comparative statistics summarised variables by schizophrenia status and assessed between-group differences. Cox proportional hazards models assessed survival, while association between schizophrenia and readmission was analysed using competing-risks regression. RESULTS: Prevalence of schizophrenia is higher in this cohort than general population, comprising 36 (19%) of 186 individuals, and 97 (30%) of 328 admissions. Those with schizophrenia were younger (66.6 vs. 72.5 years, p = 0.001), with more current smokers (75% vs. 42.7%, p = 0.005) and had admissions with shorter LOS (6 vs. 9 days, p = 0.043) and NIV duration (3 vs. 5 days, p = 0.021). There was no significant difference in reason for NIV discontinuation between the groups. Readmission rates were higher in the schizophrenia group (44.4% vs. 24.0%, p = 0.025). Age at death was lower for those with schizophrenia (67.3 vs. 77.4 years, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: People with schizophrenia had shorter LOS and NIV use, higher readmission rates, higher prevalence of current smokers and younger age at presentation and death. These findings suggest that schizophrenia is an at-risk subgroup in AHRF, highlighting the need for collaborative action.

papers.abstract_en: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a highly heterogeneous critical illness syndrome lacking effective targeted therapies, partly due to the diverse patient population. Subphenotype research aims to identify homogeneous patient subgroups sharing common biological, physiological, or clinical characteristics, enabling prognostic and predictive enrichment. This review systematically summarizes current ARDS subphenotype research, from pathobiological mechanisms to multidimensional identification based on etiology, imaging, biomarkers, respiratory mechanics, and transcriptomics. We highlight evidence for differential prognoses and treatment responses across subphenotypes, including variable effects of neuromuscular blockade, corticosteroids, and prone positioning. We further discuss challenges and future directions in translating subphenotype classification into bedside practice. This article provides a theoretical framework and practical guidance for advancing precision medicine in ARDS.

papers.abstract_en: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare, molecularly heterogeneous tumors with a complex immune microenvironment. How TAM receptor signaling interacts with STAT-SOCS-mediated immune regulation in TETs remains incompletely understood. The TAM receptor family and STAT-SOCS signaling were examined in relation to genomic alterations, gene expression, survival, and the immune microenvironment, using TCGA-THYM genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical data integrated with GTEx normal thymus expression profiles. Expression of TAM receptors (AXL, MERTK, TYRO3), their ligands (GAS6, PROS1), and the STAT1-SOCS1/SOCS3 axis was assessed using GEPIA2; survival associations were evaluated using GEPIA2 and patient-level TCGA-THYM data, and immune infiltration using TIMER2.0. Cell-type expression of TAM pathway genes was assessed using TET single-cell RNA-seq data, and protein-protein interactions using STRING. Genomic alterations affecting the TAM-STAT-SOCS axis were infrequent, comprising missense variants and copy-number amplifications. AXL, MERTK, PROS1, GAS6, STAT1, and SOCS1 showed higher expression in tumor tissues than in normal thymus. Higher MERTK expression was associated with poorer overall survival in the GEPIA2 analysis, although not significant in WHO-stratified and multivariable analyses. AXL, MERTK, and TYRO3 expression were inversely correlated with CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell infiltration, whereas GAS6, PROS1, STAT1, and SOCS3 were positively associated with neutrophil infiltration. MERTK expression was positively correlated with CD274, and single-cell analysis showed MERTK was most frequent in macrophage/monocyte populations. TAM-STAT-SOCS expression was associated with the TET immune landscape, with MERTK showing an initial association with overall survival and further associations with T-cell infiltration, CD274 expression, and cell-type-specific expression patterns.

The specific patient populations who may benefit most from surgical embolectomy are discussed. The surgical technique, using cardiopulmonary bypass, is described in detail. Special situations such as clots in transit, pregnant patients with pulmonary embolism, and the emerging role of mechanical circulatory support in the management of this condition are also discussed.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the epidemiological characteristics and coinfection of SARS-CoV-2 and influenza virus among acute respiratory infection (ARI) cases in Sichuan Province from August 2024 to July 2026. METHODS: Using 24-month surveillance data from seven national respiratory pathogen sentinel hospitals in Sichuan Province, respiratory specimens were tested for both viruses by multiplex real-time RT-PCR. Positive rates and 95% CIs were calculated by the Wilson score method; group comparisons used the chi-square test or Fisher's exact test; independent risk factors were identified by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: A total of 22,436 valid cases were included. The positive rates of SARS-CoV-2, influenza virus, and coinfection were 4.39% (95% CI: 4.13-4.67%), 9.83% (95% CI: 9.45-10.22%), and 0.05% (95% CI: 0.03-0.09%), respectively. The two viruses peaked in different seasons, with SARS-CoV-2 in summer and influenza in winter-spring. Summer was an independent risk factor for SARS-CoV-2 infection (OR = 23.88, 95% CI: 17.04-33.46); children aged 6-14 years had the highest risk of influenza (OR = 2.52, 95% CI: 2.21-2.88). The observed coinfection rate was far lower than the expectation under independent circulation of the two viruses (0.43%; O/E = 0.11, p < 0.001), indicating a negative (asynchronous) association rather than synergy, with marked spatiotemporal clustering. CONCLUSION: SARS-CoV-2 and influenza virus circulated in pronounced seasonal asynchrony in Sichuan Province, with no population-level evidence of synergy; coinfection was rare but locally clustered, supporting differentiated prevention and control strategies. Given the hospital-based sentinel design, extrapolation to the whole province should be made with caution.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Surfactant protein D (SP-D) is recognized as a potential biomarker for non-invasive evaluation of interstitial lung disease (ILD). Alterations in local and systemic cytokines associated with alveolar injury may mirror the underlying pathological processes in ILD. The study aimed to examine the correlation between plasma and sputum SP-D levels, lung function, and disease severity in patients suffering from ILD. METHODS: SP-D concentrations were evaluated in plasma and induced sputum samples from 34 healthy controls and 84 ILD patients, including 54 with systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-ILD (SARD-ILD) and 30 individuals with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Associations with pulmonary function were examined. RESULTS: ILD patients showed significantly higher SP-D than controls. Both plasma and sputum levels were elevated in IPF and SARD-ILD, with plasma SP-D higher in IPF. Plasma and sputum SP-D were moderately correlated with ILD patients (r = 0.2497, P < 0.05). Plasma SP-D was inversely associated with lung function, including reduced forced vital capacity (r=- 0.3778, P = 0.0002) and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (r=- 0.4248, P < 0.0001). These associations were significant in SARD-ILD and showed a non-significant trend in IPF. No clear link was found between sputum SP-D and pulmonary function. CONCLUSIONS: Both plasma and sputum SP-D levels were elevated in ILD patients; however, only plasma SP-D demonstrated a strong negative correlation with pulmonary function. This suggests that plasma SP-D, likely reflecting leakage from the injured lung interstitium into circulation, may serve as a practical tool for non-invasive disease severity assessment in routine clinical practice, potentially aiding in risk stratification and monitoring of disease progression.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Human ion channel genes (HICGs), as core effectors of transmembrane signal transduction, play a critical role in the initiation and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of ion channel genes in COPD. METHODS: Differential expression analysis was performed to screen HICGs in COPD datasets. A total of 107 machine learning models were employed to identify hub HICGs and evaluate their diagnostic performance, and SHAP analysis was used to assess feature contributions. GSEA, immune cell infiltration, and inflammatory cytokine correlation analyses were conducted on the hub HICGs. Consensus clustering and WGCNA were used to define two disease subtypes and key modules. Single-cell RNA-seq data were used to examine the expression patterns of the hub HICGs. Subsequently, virtual knockout, virtual drug screening, and molecular docking were performed. RESULTS: The nine hub HICGs showed high diagnostic performance in cross-dataset validation, with LRRC8D ranking first in the SHAP analysis. These HICGs were significantly correlated with immune cells and inflammatory cytokines. Consensus clustering revealed significant gender differences between the two subtypes (BH-adjusted P = 0.01), and the two subtypes were enriched in phagocytosis and MAPK signaling pathways, respectively. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis using the Ro/e index suggested enrichment of macrophages and a reduction in smooth muscle cells in the disease group. Virtual knockout of LRRC8D was predicted to preferentially affect CD68 and the affected genes were enriched in human cytomegalovirus infection. Virtual screening prioritized Tezacaftor as a potential therapeutic agent, and molecular docking predicted that Tezacaftor may exhibit high binding affinity for the hub HICGs. CONCLUSION: We identified potential HICGs in COPD and suggested a potential role for LRRC8D, as well as the potential utility of hub HICGs in disease subtyping, particularly with respect to gender, and Tezacaftor may serve as a candidate therapeutic agent.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a potentially life-threatening condition resulting from the obstruction of pulmonary arteries by embolic material, often thrombi from deep vein thrombosis of the lower extremities. This condition remains a significant public health concern, with delayed or missed diagnoses contributing to adverse health outcomes. This article aims to highlight the current standards in PE imaging, including the benefits and limitations of each modality as well as their latest advancements. The integration of advanced imaging techniques, artificial intelligence-driven image analysis, and improved perfusion assessment will continue to refine diagnostic algorithms, optimize risk stratification, and ultimately enhance patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Excessive neutrophil activation and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation contribute to hyperinflammation and disruption of the alveolar capillary barrier in acute lung injury (ALI). C5a/C5aR1 signaling links complement activation to neutrophil migration, Ca2+ mobilization, ROS production, and NET formation. This study investigated whether Shengjiang San (SJS) regulates these responses in ALI and explored candidate circulating constituents. METHODS: ALI was induced in mice by intratracheal LPS administration, and SJS treatment was initiated before LPS exposure. Lung injury, barrier integrity, neutrophil responses, NET formation, C5a/C5aR1 changes, and lung transcriptomic profiles were assessed. Purified murine neutrophils were stimulated with C5a or PMA to evaluate the effects of SJS-containing serum. Serum pharmacochemistry, plasma exposure analysis, biolayer interferometry, molecular docking, and neutrophil assays were used to characterize ferulic acid. RESULTS: SJS reduced pulmonary inflammation, edema, vascular leakage, neutrophil accumulation and activation, and NET formation, while preserving the integrity of the alveolar capillary barrier. Transcriptomic profiling showed enrichment of complement activation, neutrophil activation, and NET formation among genes differentially expressed between the SJS and Model groups. SJS also lowered C5a concentrations in plasma and lung homogenates and reduced pulmonary C5aR1 expression. In neutrophils, SJS-containing serum significantly suppressed C5a-stimulated neutrophil functions, including migration, Ca2+ flux, oxidative burst, and NET release, while PMX205 produced a similar inhibitory pattern. SJS-containing serum also inhibited PMA-induced NET formation. Ferulic acid was detected in serum as a prototype constituent with measurable plasma exposure, showed concentration-dependent binding to recombinant human C5a with an apparent K D of 21.65 μM, and reduced histone H3 citrullination and NET formation in C5a-stimulated neutrophils. CONCLUSION: SJS attenuated LPS-induced ALI and restrained neutrophil activation and NET formation mediated by C5a/C5aR1 signaling. Ferulic acid was identified as a candidate circulating constituent that reduced C5a-activated NET formation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Vaccination and natural infection with Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome CoronaVirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) confer immune protection through distinct mechanisms, however, their effects on Natural Killer (NK) cell responses remain poorly understood, particularly in relation to COVID-19 disease severity. NK cells, key mediators of anti-viral immunity, have been implicated in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pathogenesis, where severe disease is associated with hyperactivated yet dysfunctional NK-cell states that likely impair viral control and contribute to tissue damage. METHODS: To define how vaccination and infection shape NK-cell biology, we performed longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of NK cells from SARS-CoV-2-naïve individuals receiving two doses of the BNT162b2mRNA vaccine. These longitudinal vaccine profiles were integrated with cross-sectional scRNA-seq datasets from unvaccinated patients with acute COVID-19 and from independent convalescent individuals, all enrolled before vaccine introduction. RESULTS: We identified distinct NK cell transcriptional programs associated with vaccination, acute infection and convalescence, with the most pronounced infection-related alterations observed in the severe form of the disease. These diverging transcriptional signatures correlate with differences in NK-cell subset composition and activation markers between vaccinated and infected individuals. CONCLUSIONS: Taken together, these findings provide a rationale for future studies examining whether vaccine-associated NK-cell transcriptional programs contribute to durable immune protection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute viral infections trigger overlapping but virus-specific blood transcriptional responses; however, current analyses rarely quantify the mechanistic depth of activation across pathways, regulators, and immune cell compositions. METHODS: RNA-seq data from GSE157240 were reanalyzed to infer transcription factor (TF) activity using DoRothEA/decoupleR, signaling pathway activity using PROGENy, and stress pathway and transcriptional perturbation breadth metrics. These four components were integrated into a viral host perturbation score (VHPS), a proof-of-concept framework designed to quantify the magnitude of host transcriptional perturbation. Differential expression analysis, Gene Ontology enrichment, module scoring, and CIBERSORTx-based immune deconvolution were used to compare respiratory and systemic viral infections. RESULTS: VHPS-stratified viruses along an axis of host transcriptional perturbation, with DNA viruses showing the highest median perturbation, followed by dengue and enterovirus/rhinovirus, whereas influenza A and other respiratory RNA viruses were intermediate and healthy controls were lowest. Upregulated genes revealed virus-specific and shared signatures, and immune/stress GO terms showed stronger T cell and interferon enrichment for respiratory viruses. A 26-gene "shared respiratory antiviral" module correlated with VHPS and TF/stress components but not PROGENy activity. Immune deconvolution revealed virus-specific leukocyte remodeling, with marked Treg depletion and elevated neutrophils in respiratory viruses, monocyte skewing in dengue, and the lowest Treg fractions in DNA viruses. CONCLUSIONS: Together, VHPS and immune deconvolution delineate shared and virus-specific regulatory programs in acute viral infections, but the generalizability of VHPS requires evaluation in independent datasets.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with right ventricular failure, from increased pulmonary vascular resistance due to thrombus obstruction and hypoxia-induced vasoconstriction, driving adverse outcomes in intermediate-high and high-risk presentations. Despite advances in imaging and therapeutic technology, guidance on escalation beyond anticoagulation is limited, and management strategies continue to vary widely across institutions. The Pulmonary Embolism Response Team model was developed to address these gaps through real-time multidisciplinary evaluation and individualized treatment decisions. This article summarizes the evolution of evidence and guideline recommendations shaping contemporary PE care.

It reviews how advancements in medical and device therapies have shaped treatment selection while highlighting persistent evidence gaps. Across decades of trials, the primary challenge remains achieving balance between effective reperfusion with optimization of safety outcomes and clinical benefit.
